title: Dispatch: ammunition expenditure and recovery (attempt 1)
description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4`). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR for eight beads); your branch already contains migrations 0032 and 0033 — the next contiguous migration number is 0034. Read AGENTS.md; docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5; ADR 0020 §§2-3; the inventory modules under packages/core/src/state/ (inventoryLifecycle.ts, inventoryWorldLocation.ts, inventoryIdentity.ts, itemTransfer.ts) and the remove_item / claim_item / list_recoverable_items tools.

SOURCE (SRD rule:weapon-properties, Ammunition): "You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack ... At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield." SRD division rule: round down.

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0034_ammunition_expenditure.sql: table ammunition_expenditure (campaign_id, expenditure_id TEXT PK, combat_instance_id TEXT NOT NULL, character_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_inventory_id TEXT NOT NULL (the held stack spent from), expended_inventory_id TEXT NOT NULL (the unheld dropped row holding the spent pieces), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK > 0, world_location_id TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('expended','resolved'), provenance, session_id, created_at, resolved_at). Indexes for (campaign_id, combat_instance_id, character_id). Follow ADR 0015 conventions; regenerate the schema snapshot (`npm run -w @eshyra/core schema:snapshot`); document the table in schema.ts comments.
2. New tool `expend_ammunition` (mutates) { itemId, quantity? (default 1, integer >= 1), character? }: requires an ACTIVE combat instance (the battle); requires the item to be a held row of the character with quantity >= quantity. It moves `quantity` pieces out of custody exactly as remove_item with disposition 'dropped' does for a partial stack (reuse that code path, do not duplicate it), at the character's current world location, and records an expenditure row linked to the active instance, in one transaction. Whether the item is the right ammunition for the weapon stays DM interpretation; the tool does not resolve attacks.
3. New tool `recover_ammunition` (mutates) { combatInstanceId, character? }: allowed only when that combat instance is CLOSED (the end of the battle) and the campaign's current location equals the expenditures' world location; refused if the character has no 'expended' rows for that instance. For each ammunition identity (group by the identity the inventory code already uses to merge stacks), N = total expended pieces still present in their expended rows (pieces another tool already moved, e.g. via claim_item or destroy, are not counted — report them); recoverable = floor(N / 2). In one transaction: return `recoverable` pieces to the character's custody (merge into a matching held stack when the inventory code supports merging, else claim/split rows), destroy the remaining unrecovered pieces of those expended rows, and mark the expenditure rows 'resolved'. Second call for the same instance/character is refused. The tool does not advance the clock (the minute of searching is the DM's narrative time).
4. Descriptions: contracts only. expend_ammunition: call after each attack with an ammunition weapon (one piece per attack), only during combat. recover_ammunition: after the battle's combat instance is closed, recovers half (rounded down) of the pieces still lying where they were expended and destroys the rest. No arithmetic for the model.
5. Known limit rule:weapon-properties (ruleKnownLimits.ts), R0 re-derivation: rewrite to the bounded statement (resolve_check does not spend ammunition; for a character, spend with expend_ammunition after each attack with an ammunition weapon and recover with recover_ammunition after the battle; loading restriction stays). Remove remove_item/claim_item from it if no longer named; participants list exactly the tools named. Remove 'ammunition-recovery-count' from its capabilityGaps and from ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS (delete the field if no gap remains). Update the identity-pinned gapsByKey map and the ammunition assertions in packages/core/test/rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts (replace, do not just delete; the old 'no tool determines how many' assertion becomes an assertion on the new tools). Keep the 8-word source-restatement test green. Design doc A5 table: note the ammunition-recovery-count gap as landed in eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4.
6. If any existing out-of-combat flow needs ammunition spending, that is NOT this capability: the source's recovery rule is about battles. State in the expend_ammunition description that it requires an active combat instance.

TESTS (state module + tool registry): expend splits correctly and records; refused without active combat / insufficient quantity / not held; recovery: N=1→0, N=2→1, N=7→3, two ammunition types, pieces moved away before recovery not counted, wrong location refused, instance still active refused, second call refused, unrecovered pieces destroyed, recovered pieces back in custody with identity preserved.

OUT OF SCOPE: monster ammunition; attack resolution; anything not listed.

TEST COVERAGE IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE: write every test listed under TESTS (one `it` per bullet at minimum), driven through the real tool registry wherever the behaviour is model-facing. The supervisor reviews the test list against this spec and rejects under-tested work. In your completion notes, map each TESTS bullet to the test name that covers it.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation per the description on its own branch; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
notes:
Dispatched gpt-6-luna high, pgid 2512604, off eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8@0d5ad3cd.
Completion report (commit 1111bc2e). Files: migration 0034 and schema snapshot/comment; state ammunition expenditure and recovery operations; expend_ammunition and recover_ammunition registry tools; weapon-properties known-limit rewrite, A5 design table, registry/migration expectations, and ammunition tests. Decisions: implemented the supervisor design as written; expenditure reuses removeItem dropped-stack behavior inside the enclosing transaction; no stack-merge operation exists, so recovery claims or splits exact-identity rows; no design deviation was forced by the code. TESTS map: expend splits and records -> expend_ammunition splits a partial stack and records its active combat row; no active combat -> refuses expenditure without an active combat instance; insufficient quantity -> refuses expenditure greater than the held quantity; not held -> refuses expenditure from an item not held by the target character; N=1 to 0 -> recovers zero of N=1 and destroys the unrecovered piece; N=2 to 1 -> recovers one of N=2; N=7 to 3 -> recovers three of N=7 using round-down division; separate types -> computes recovery separately for two ammunition identities; previously moved pieces excluded and reported -> does not count an expended row claimed before recovery; wrong location -> refuses recovery at a different current location; active instance refused -> refuses recovery while the combat instance remains active; repeat call refused -> refuses a second recovery call for the same character and instance; unrecovered pieces destroyed -> recovers zero of N=1 and destroys the unrecovered piece; recovered custody and identity -> returns recovered pieces to character custody with exact inventory identity. Rule statement and gap retirement -> preserves the bounded knockout, ready, water, and ammunition known limits; registry names -> lists the default tool set and exposes provider-neutral definitions. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed: format/check, forced typecheck, 318 test files passed, 2 skipped; 5,620 passed, 3 skipped.
